title: Nested structures and arrays of structures
learningObjectives: Explain the C concept and its rules.
Trace the example and describe data flow.
Identify relevant failure and boundary cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A structure member may itself be a structure, and an array may contain multiple structure objects. Member access can therefore be chained with dot operators and array subscripting.
understand.whyItMatters: Nested structures represent related entities without flattening every field into one large record. Arrays of structures support collections of records with consistent layout.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
A structure member may itself be a structure, and an array may contain multiple structure objects. Member access can therefore be chained with dot operators and array subscripting.

Check all return values, object lifetimes, types and preconditions. Enable compiler warnings and test expected as well as failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: tickets is an array of two Ticket structures. Each Ticket contains an embedded Date structure, accessed through tickets[i].opened.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the access path to the month of the second ticket.
practise.independentTask: Create an array of five student records, each containing a nested date structure, and print a selected field.
hints: Use braces that reflect the nested aggregate structure when initializing.
An embedded structure member is part of the containing object; it is not a separately allocated pointer.
Validate values such as dates when the application requires semantic correctness.
